vocabularyDefinition.en: Institutions are the actual interpretation of a product or service. The competent authority can vary: federal, Flemish, provincial,... And the service can be provided by another government such as a local government. A government service is a mandatory or optional set of activities that are or may be carried out by or on behalf of a public organisation, publicly funded and arising from public policy. Services may benefit an individual, an organisation or association, a company or other public authority, or groups of any of these parties. A service exists regardless of whether it is used or not. According to the revised European Interoperability Framework, a European public service includes any service provided by public authorities in Europe, or by other organisations on their behalf, to businesses, citizens or other public authorities.

vocabularyDefinition.en: The services provided by local authorities are often based on Flemish, federal or European legislation, which is translated to a local level. This means that the basis is the same for every local government, but that there may be flexibility for the local interpretation. Because we want to get and keep IPDC well stocked and up to date, with a limited administrative burden, we provide the concept. A draft is a template that editors of the Flemish government prepare for local authorities. It contains a general interpretation of a government service, which can also be applicable in most local contexts. Local authorities can consult these concepts and decide to register their own services on the basis of a concept. At that moment, a concept is cloned to an authority. The local government can then fully adapt this body and tailor it to the local context. In this way, a concept also groups together all the different local variations of a similar service.
